title: The Last Protocol Anew
premise: Casper Iversen is a clone of a murdered courier, legally erased but still running the original's route between two star systems locked in a cold truce. When the manifest of a decommissioned ship lists a name that shouldn't exist — her own, in the original's handwriting — she uncovers evidence that the murder was staged to hide a peace protocol both fleets want buried. Hunted by the original's killers and shadowed by an investigator who may be another copy of herself, Casper must choose which identity to be when she delivers the message. In the end she broadcasts the protocol from neutral space as herself, not the original, forcing both fleets to accept peace on terms that name her — and sentencing her to exile that feels, for once, like freedom.
about_author: Mirabel Marchetti is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade of logging transmissions no one answered. She writes about people who carry messages across distances that were never meant to be crossed.

chapters.title: Dead Letter Lane
chapters.summary: POV Casper. On the hauler Vesperine, Casper runs contraband mail between the warring systems of Calloway and Threnody, invisible by design. A routine pickup includes a sealed packet addressed to 'C. Iversen' — the original's name, not hers. The beat: unease beneath routine; someone knows what she is.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Cross-checking port records, Casper finds the packet listed on the manifest of the Halcyon Drift, a ship destroyed nine years ago with the original Iversen aboard. Her own face stares back from the crew registry. Beat: dread hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: POV Casper. She opens the packet: half a cipher key and a note in the original's handwriting, dated after his death. A dockside informant warns her that a fleet auditor has been asking about clone couriers. Beat: the past stops being past.

chapters.title: Auditor at the Airlock
chapters.summary: POV Sefa Rennick, fleet investigator. Rennick boards the Vesperine under truce-inspection authority, hunting the murdered courier's estate. She interviews Casper and notes small wrongnesses — a scar that healed differently, a gait too careful. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Rennick suspects but can't prove.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Casper, flashback-heavy. We learn how clones are legally voided, how Casper bought the original's route and silence, and why she never asked who killed him. Beat: sympathy deepens; invisibility revealed as wound, not strategy.

chapters.title: The Cipher Half
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Working the partial key against old route logs, Casper finds it matches coordinates along the war's first battle line. Someone wanted the original to deliver something there — something worth killing him for. Beat: purpose kindles inside fear.

chapters.title: What the Truce Buys
chapters.summary: POV Rennick. Rennick reports to Admiral Okonjo, who orders her to find and quietly destroy any 'Iversen material' before the truce expires in forty days. Rennick realizes she's working for a cover-up, not justice. Beat: moral fracture in the antagonist.

chapters.title: Ghosts on the Line
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At a derelict relay station on the old battle line, Casper recovers a black box: the Halcyon Drift didn't explode — it was scuttled by its own escort, and the original recorded it. Beat: grief and fury fused; the case becomes hers.

chapters.title: Two of a Kind
chapters.summary: POV Rennick. Rennick corners Casper at a neutral port — and reveals she is also a clone of the original, grown by the fleet as an internal witness. She offers Casper safety in exchange for the black box. Beat: identity crisis doubled; trust impossible, kinship undeniable.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Decoding further, they find a third entry on the Halcyon manifest: 'M. Adeyemi, protocol bearer' — alive, hidden, holding the other half of the key. Rennick hesitates over betraying Okonjo. Beat: reluctant alliance forms.

chapters.title: Forty Days
chapters.summary: POV Rennick. Okonjo, sensing defection, strips Rennick's clearance and puts a bounty on both women. Rennick chooses Casper over the fleet, burning her career to warn her. Beat: the antagonist becomes an ally; stakes go personal.

chapters.title: Running the Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A chase chapter across three ports as bounty crews close in; Casper uses every dead drop and forged seal the original left her. They escape with minutes to spare but lose the black box. Beat: exhaustion, competence, mounting desperation.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Casper. They trace M. Adeyemi to a hospice moon where the old diplomat lives incognito, dying. Adeyemi confirms the protocol: mutual disarmament terms both fleets' hawks buried with the Halcyon. Beat: hope arrives wearing mortality's face.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Rennick. Rennick confesses why she took the auditor post: she was grown to testify against the original and failed him. Casper must decide whether Rennick's guilt earns forgiveness or is just another survival strategy. Beat: theme crystallized — identity as choice, not origin.

chapters.title: Half a Key Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Adeyemi dies mid-transfer, leaving them the protocol but not the authentication both fleets will demand. Without it, broadcasting the message could trigger the war instead of ending it. Beat: the plan's fatal flaw exposed; despair.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Re-reading the note dated after death, Casper realizes the original anticipated his murder and hid the second key fragment inside his own memorial vault on Calloway — the one place no one would look. Beat: the dead mentor speaks; resolve returns.

chapters.title: Homecoming of a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper infiltrates Calloway during a fleet ceremony honoring the Halcyon dead, walking openly through the city that voided her. She retrieves the fragment from the vault as the honor guard approaches. Beat: terror transfigured into claim-staking; she exists.

chapters.title: Truce Expiring
chapters.summary: POV Rennick. With six days left, border skirmishes begin; Okonjo moves to manufacture a casus belli. Rennick steals the fleet's own authentication codes to complete the pair. Beat: ticking clock made audible; betrayal of the fleet completed.

chapters.title: Neutral Ground
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The three converge at the derelict relay station — Casper, Rennick, and the message — just as Okonjo's strike team arrives. A standoff in vacuum suits among the wreckage of the Halcyon Drift. Beat: climax ignites; everything on the line.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Under fire, Casper transmits the full authenticated protocol on all bands, signing it with her own name and Rennick's — not the original's. Crews on both sides receive orders to stand down alongside proof their hawks falsified the war's cause. Beat: climax resolved through identity claimed, not hidden.

chapters.title: After the Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Rennick. Both fleets convene emergency councils; Okonjo is arrested by her own officers. Rennick testifies publicly as a clone and survives it — barely. Beat: justice outside the law achieved at cost; the world rearranges.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Opened
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Months later, the corridors between Calloway and Threnody reopen. Casper takes a legitimate mail contract under her own name, Rennick riding shotgun. The last line: some messages are only deliverable by the person you decide to become. Beat: quiet, earned resolution.
